content.statement: Cat in a box is in superposition |cat⟩ = (|alive⟩ + |dead⟩)/√2.
content.explanation: Paradox: cat seems both alive and dead until observed. Highlights the measurement problem.

Know what problem or physical phenomenon 23.1 Schrödinger's Cat addresses.

from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
from qiskit.quantum_info import Statevector
import json

content.explanation: P(t) = |⟨ψ(0)|ψ(t)⟩|² ≈ 1 − (ΔH)² t². With measurements every τ, P(nτ) ≈ (1 − (ΔH)²τ²)ⁿ → 1 as τ→0. Applications: state preservation.
keyTakeaways: Frequent measurement prevents evolution.

Know what problem or physical phenomenon 23.9 Bell's Theorem addresses.

steps.title: Define correlations
steps.text: Correlation is the average product of the two ±1 outcomes.

steps.title: Combine four settings
steps.text: CHSH combines four correlations into one test statistic.

steps.title: Compare bounds
steps.text: Quantum theory predicts values that can exceed the local bound.

codeExamples.code:
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
from qiskit.quantum_info import Statevector
import json

LESSON_ID = '23-23-9-bell-s-theorem'
circuit = QuantumCircuit(2)
circuit.h(0)
circuit.cx(0, 1)
circuit.measure_all()
from qiskit.primitives import StatevectorSampler
sampler = StatevectorSampler(seed=7)
result = sampler.run([circuit], shots=1024).result()
print(json.dumps({'lesson': LESSON_ID, 'counts': result[0].data.meas.get_counts()}))

content.statement: GHZ state gives a single-shot contradiction with local realism.
content.explanation: For |GHZ⟩ = (|000⟩+|111⟩)/√2, measuring X or Y on each qubit. Classical prediction: product of outcomes = +1; quantum prediction: product = −1. No statistics needed.
keyTakeaways: GHZ state gives a single-shot contradiction with local realism.
